newsitem.title: USA: U.S. regrets failure of UN motion on China rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. regrets failure of UN motion on China rights.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright expressed regret over the failure of a Western resolution at the U.N. human rights commission criticising China's human rights record.

"We regret that decision," Albright said in a speech at the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis, Md. The United States had been a co-sponsor of the resolution, which was proposed by Denmark, at the meeting of the commission in Geneva.
"We congratulate the government of Denmark for sponsoring the resolution and the others who co-sponsored it," Albright said.

For the seventh year since 1990, Western European countries and the United States failed to achieve even a vote on the issue in the 53-member body despite heavy lobbying, handing China a diplomatic triumph.
The Chinese delegation won a vote for a so-called "no-action motion" on the issue by 27 against 17 with nine countries, including Russia, abstaining, effectively blocking scrutiny of its record.
